r14-b2-refix.title: Rework 1: B2 refix + symmetric-boundary scope addition
r14-b2-refix.imperative: Re-verify the path-boundary predicate with independent exploits from both ends; specifically test whether the trailing character class over-rejects legitimate prose shapes, and hunt for a third hole.
r14-b2-refix.finding: B2 CLEARED and the scope addition is sound. 34 independent probes against _appears_at_path_boundary. Both named defect classes are closed: suffix-of-a-longer-path (my round-1 h1_substring.json now exits 1, naming the offender) and trailing-glued extension (.bak, -old, _v2, /child, .5 all correctly rejected). OVER-REJECTION, the Commander's explicit question: NO defect. All 15 legitimate shapes accepted - start-of-string, whitespace, backtick, paren, single and double quote, sentence-final period, comma, semicolon, colon, question mark, newline, end-of-string, possessive 's, and a bounded second occurrence after an unbounded first. The '.'-disambiguation earns its keep and is correctly documented. Three edge over-rejections, all conservative and all loud: './refs/a.md' prefix form, 'refs/a.md-derived' hyphenated English, and 'refs/a.md.then' (a typo shape). None silent, none present in the corpus. THIRD HOLE, as asked: the trailing rule is a deny-list, so any character that continues a filename but is not in [A-Za-z0-9_/\-] and is not '.'+alnum reads as a boundary. Exploitable: docs/x.md._old, docs/x.md.~1~, docs/x.md..bak, docs/x.md(2), docs/x.md:stream, and any non-ASCII glued suffix (docs/x.mdé) - each accepted though it names a different file. Strictly smaller than B2, exotic in an ASCII markdown/JSON corpus, and the principled tightening is to invert the trailing rule to a punctuation allow-list. NOT worth a third block. Shipped spine lints clean (0 offenders) and default discovery over the whole corpus is clean (13 checklists).
